prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map separates the five garage views into broad distance layers: the camera wearer’s hands and forearms are nearest, roughly 0.2–0.7 m away, the yellow machine is about 0.8–2 m ahead, and the floor, benches, and another partly cropped person are generally farther away, about 2–4 m. Across the frames, the machine shifts from the upper-left/right periphery toward the center and becomes larger and brighter, consistent with the wearer approaching and turning toward it; nearby arms increasingly occlude its controls and frame. It reveals depth ordering and the shapes of overlapping machine parts more clearly than RGB, including hands lying in front of the machine and the floor extending behind it. Exact metric distances are uncertain, and several regions look unreliable: bright distant structures merge with near objects, dark holes appear around thin parts and boundaries, and brightness is not fully consistent between frames.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map mainly isolates people and portions of the yellow machine against black, showing the wearer’s hands/arms growing from small lower-edge regions into large foreground masks as the camera approaches the machine. The wearer’s limbs are within arm’s reach of the machine, approximately 0.2–0.8 m from it, while the other person appears only as a small, partly out-of-frame region several metres ahead in the first view and cannot be tracked reliably afterward. The masks clarify which foreground regions occlude the machine and show that much of the machine remains above and in front of the wearer, but they provide little direct depth, facing, gaze, or separation information without the RGB and depth map. Reliability is poor: machine regions are inconsistently labeled as “motorcycle,” unrelated areas are labeled “banana,” several people masks appear spurious or fused with arms, and most floor, bench, tools, and machine structure are omitted.
descriptions.pose: The pose map detects mostly hands: small hand skeletons appear near the lower centre in the earlier usable frame, paired hands appear roughly 0.3–0.6 m in front of the wearer around the middle frame, and later frames show hands spread across the centre and right while a partial yellow upper-body chain enters from below. It makes hand placement and articulation easier to distinguish than RGB, showing the hands above or in front of the machine and revealing when one hand is farther right or higher than the other; the hands remain within the wearer’s reach and often overlap or occlude machine components. The changing skeleton locations support camera turning and approach toward the machine, but no complete second-person skeleton is available, so another person’s facing direction, gaze toward the wearer, or reach cannot be established. The map is unreliable in the first two frames and near image boundaries, where detections are absent, duplicated, fragmented, or reduced to isolated keypoints, and it provides no dependable metric depth by itself.
